claims.text: Role in pheo: surgery is delayed until HTN is controlled w alpha- + beta-blockers, usually phenoxybenzamine 20 to 40 mg PO 3 times a day;
claims.quote: The operation is usually delayed until hypertension is controlled by a combination of alpha-blockers and beta-blockers (usually phenoxybenzamine 20 to 40 mg orally 3 times a day
The blood pressure target is < 130/80 mmHg

claims.text: blockade is presumed effective after ~10 to 14 days (CV re-equilibration);
claims.quote: Re-equilibration of the cardiovascular system requires approximately 10 to 14 days, after which blockade is presumed to be effective.

claims.text: intraop hypertensive paroxysms: phentolamine 1 to 5 mg IV or nitroprusside infusion.
claims.quote: paroxysms of hypertension should be controlled with injections of phentolamine 1 to 5 mg IV or nitroprusside infusion (2 to 4 mcg/kg/minute)

claims.text: Phenoxybenzamine (Dibenzyline) dose, pheochromocytoma: Initially 10 mg twice a day.
claims.quote: Initially, 10 mg of phenoxybenzamine hydrochloride twice a day.

claims.text: Increase every other day, usually to 20 to 40 mg 2 or 3 times a day, until optimal (BP control).
claims.quote: Dosage should be increased every other day, usually to 20 to 40 mg 2 or 3 times a day, until an optimal dosage is obtained, as judged by blood pressure control.

claims.text: Start small and ↑ slowly until the desired effect or side effects from blockade become troublesome.
claims.quote: Small initial doses should be slowly increased until the desired effect is obtained or the side effects from blockade become troublesome.

claims.text: Phenoxybenzamine (Dibenzyline) safety: CI: conditions where a fall in BP may be undesirable; hypersensitivity to the drug or any of its components.
claims.quote: Conditions where a fall in blood pressure may be undesirable; hypersensitivity to the drug or any of its components.

claims.text: Alpha blockade leaves beta receptors unopposed; compounds that stimulate both receptor types may produce an exaggerated hypotensive response and tachycardia.
claims.quote: Phenoxybenzamine hydrochloride-induced alpha-adrenergic blockade leaves beta-adrenergic receptors unopposed. Compounds that stimulate both types of receptors may, therefore, produce an exaggerated hypotensive response and tachycardia.

claims.text: May interact w/ epinephrine to produce an exaggerated hypotensive response and tachycardia.
claims.quote: Phenoxybenzamine hydrochloride may interact with compounds that stimulate both alpha- and beta-adrenergic receptors (i.e., epinephrine) to produce an exaggerated hypotensive response and tachycardia.

claims.text: Case reports of carcinoma in humans after long-term tx; long-term use not recommended.
claims.quote: Case reports of carcinoma in humans after long-term treatment with phenoxybenzamine have been reported. Hence long-term use of phenoxybenzamine is not recommended.

claims.text: Use w/ caution in marked cerebral or coronary arteriosclerosis or renal damage; blocking effect may aggravate symptoms of respiratory infections.
claims.quote: Administer with caution in patients with marked cerebral or coronary arteriosclerosis or renal damage. Adrenergic blocking effect may aggravate symptoms of respiratory infections.

claims.text: Adverse reactions: postural hypotension, tachycardia, inhibition of ejaculation, nasal congestion, miosis.
claims.quote: Postural hypotension, tachycardia, inhibition of ejaculation, nasal congestion, miosis.

claims.text: OD Sx: postural hypotension w/ dizziness or fainting, tachycardia (esp postural), vomiting, lethargy, shock.
claims.quote: They may include postural hypotension, resulting in dizziness or fainting; tachycardia, particularly postural; vomiting; lethargy; shock.

claims.text: OD tx: discontinue the drug; treatment of circulatory failure is a prime consideration.
claims.quote: When symptoms and signs of overdosage exist, discontinue the drug. Treatment of circulatory failure, if present, is a prime consideration.

claims.text: Epinephrine is contraindicated in OD (net effect is vasodilation and a further drop in BP: epinephrine reversal).
claims.quote: Epinephrine is contraindicated because it stimulates both alpha- and beta-receptors; since alpha-receptors are blocked, the net effect of epinephrine administration is vasodilation and a further drop in blood pressure (epinephrine reversal).

claims.text: IV levarterenol bitartrate may be used for severe hypotensive reactions (stimulates alpha-receptors primarily).
claims.quote: I.V. Infusion of levarterenol bitartrate** may be used to combat severe hypotensive reactions, because it stimulates alpha-receptors primarily.
